newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall from high, seen extending dip.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall from high, seen extending dip.

text.p: Polish shares on Tuesday fell in a profit-taking correction which may have been hastened by the central bank's Monday decision to raise mandatory reserves on zloty call deposits and on currency deposits, analysts said.
They said the main market, which had risen to a 33-month high at 16,910.4 points on Monday, could fall for the next few sessions toward 16,000 points before rebounding.

"It seems we've had a technical correction helped by the decision by the National Bank of Poland (the central bank) to lift the level of obligatory reserves," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

Some analysts said the obligatory reserve decision to limit money supply could help slow growth and thereby hurt stocks, while others said mostly banks could suffer, as they would be forced to give over greater amounts to reserves.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.4 percent to 16,679.6 points and turnover fell 9.5 percent to 222.3 million zlotys ($73.8 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 50 to 19 with 17 stocks flat.
Analysts said a good sign was that smaller stocks showed greater falls, which were in low trade.

Analysts said top gainer garment maker Prochnik surged 9.7 percent after a district court cleared the sale of a 10 percent stake to a National Investment Fund (NFI) in Poland's mass privatisation programme.
Recent big gainers computer maker Optimus and trader Universal fell 4.7 percent and 3.5 percent respectively in heavy trade due to profit-taking, analysts said.

NFI units fell 1.9 percent in the regular session and fell 0.7 percent in 27.7-million-zloty ($9.2 million) continuous trade, where nine stocks fell, three rose and four were flat in 14.3-million-zloty ($4.7 million) trade.
